newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian bishops tell politicians ensure democracy.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian bishops tell politicians ensure democracy.

text.p: Nigerian Catholic bishops on Tuesday urged the nation's politicians to show they were capable of ruling and to make the on-going transition to civil rule programme of the military rulers successful.

"The main actors in the government's transition programme need to take their minds away from the military to ensure Nigeria returns to civilian rule in 1998," said a statement issued by the bishops after their annual conference in Lagos.
"The political parties should see how they can make the transition plan of (military ruler) General Sani Abacha work to prove people wrong that they are incapable of holding their own," it said.
Abacha is implementing a plan of phased elections he says will lead to his hand over of power to a democratically-elected president in October 1998.
Municipal polls are due on March 15 while a 10-day voters registration exercise dogged by numerous problems including fraud and inadequate materials ended last Wednesday.
Critics of the government, however, dismiss the transition plan as a ruse, saying Abacha intends to use it to succeed himself.
Some politicians have been urging Abacha to contest next year's presidential election and the bishops said this was an admission of the failure of the political class to rule.
"The political class appear incapable of holding their own," said Father Matthew Kukah, secretary-general of the Catholic secretariat in Lagos.
"Most of them are sycophants parleying with the military authorities as if they need the help of the army to fulfil their own political ambitions," he told Reuters.
Africa's most populous country has been in crisis since 1993 when a presidential vote to restore democracy was annulled.

Abacha seized power in the aftermath of the chaos unleashed by the annulment and despite the transition programme, Moshood Abiola, the presumed winner of the poll remains in detention since 1994 when he was held for proclaiming himself president.
Nigeria has been under fire from home and abroad for alleged human rights abuses and lack of democracy.
